channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Chess Team Secures Second Gold Medal at FIDE Olympiad
item.description: Uzbekistan's national chess team won its second gold medal at the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, losing only one match. Star player Javokhir Sindarov will challenge the world champion in November. The team, including top-ranked players like Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Nodirbek Yakubboev, defeated strong opponents such as India, China, and the United States.

item.title: US Promotes Small Nuclear Reactor Technology in Caucasus and Central Asia
item.description: The United States is actively promoting its small modular nuclear reactor (SMR) technology in the Caucasus and Central Asia. US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Shawna J. Wilson met with Armenian and Kazakh officials to discuss nuclear cooperation. Both countries have shown openness to the idea, with Armenia finalizing a deal and Kazakhstan signing an agreement for training assistance.

item.title: Almaty Court Hears of Suspect Linked to Sanctions Evasion in Theft Case
item.description: During a trial in Almaty, a witness emerged who was linked to an investigation into evading sanctions against Russia. The witness's company was involved in supplying industrial equipment. The court is hearing testimony in a case involving alleged embezzlement of 42 million tenge related to an auto race organization.

item.title: China and Middle East Establish Investment Fund for Central Asia
item.description: China, Oman, Turkey, and Uzbekistan are launching the CACPEF fund to invest in companies in Central Asia and the Caucasus. Participants include China Investment Corporation, Oman Investment Authority, Uzbekistan's Fund for Reconstruction and Development, Turkey's OYAK, and the Eurasian Development Bank. The fund aims to provide businesses with access to technology, expertise, and new markets, strengthening regional economic ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pursues Economic Diplomacy Through International Engagements
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its economic diplomacy by engaging with its embassies and consulates abroad. Recent activities include graduates of the 'Water for All' program in France receiving diplomas, Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General's Office studying counter-terrorism methods in the UK, a business forum held with Poland, and educational cooperation discussions with Serbia. Singapore hosted an event celebrating Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, highlighting trade and cultural ties.

item.title: Russian Doctors Arrive in Uzbekistan for 'Mission of Kindness' Program
item.description: Seven specialists from RZD-Medicine have arrived in Uzbekistan for the international volunteer mission 'Mission of Kindness,' running from October 26-31. The Russian doctors are holding professional meetings with Uzbek colleagues, sharing expertise, and providing consultations. The delegation includes specialists in cardiology, oncology, urology, gynecology, ophthalmology, and traumatology, visiting medical centers in Tashkent and Samarkand.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Turkey for Official Visit, Met by President Erdoğan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Turkey for an official visit. He was personally welcomed at Ankara's Etimesgut Airport by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. A guard of honor was present, and the leaders held a brief conversation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements Targeted Social Support Programs for Vulnerable Populations
item.description: Bukhara region is systematically supporting vulnerable groups, including people with disabilities, the elderly, women, and children. Over 9 months, 514 social workers provided 120 types of services. The 'Sahovat va Kumak' Fund disbursed 12.7 billion soms for treatment, medicine, and housing repairs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks in Top 50 Countries for Public Safety
item.description: Kazakhstan has secured 41st place out of 143 countries in the 'Public Order and Safety' index of the World Justice Project's Rule of Law Index for 2026. The country has improved its position for the third consecutive year, ranking above France, Italy, Portugal, Georgia, Turkey, and Russia.

item.title: OSCE Assists Water Quality Monitoring in Syr Darya River Basin
item.description: The OSCE project coordinator in Uzbekistan, in collaboration with the National Center for Environmental Monitoring, is supporting water quality monitoring in the Syr Darya river basin. The initiative aims to identify pollution sources, assess environmental risks, and enhance cooperation in water resource management. Chemical analysis of surface waters and sediments is being conducted.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Spiritual Directorate Denies Ties to Accused Religious Figure
item.description: The Spiritual Directorate of Muslims of Kazakhstan (SDMK) has issued a statement regarding the controversy surrounding religious figure Ismatulla Maksum, who is accused of sexually harassing minors. The SDMK stated that Maksum and his followers have no affiliation with the directorate and their actions do not align with its principles. The directorate emphasized that violence, intimidation, and coercion are grave sins in Islam.

item.title: Uzbek Company Aims to Compete with Foreign Firms in Mining Sector
item.description: Sherzod Isokhonov, Executive Director of 'Shark Shakht Kurish,' stated that the company, founded in 2023, is focused on comprehensive mine design, construction, and modernization. With over 180 employees and operations dating back to 2009, the company believes it can compete with international players by leveraging local expertise and expanding global connections.

item.title: Hazara Representatives Denounce Persecution and Rights Violations in Afghanistan
item.description: Hazara community representatives condemned ethnic and religious persecution, forced displacement, and land grabbing in Afghanistan. They highlighted ongoing oppression and expressed concerns over restrictions on women, activists, and media. The group warned the Taliban of potential consequences for continued discrimination and rights violations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Freedom Holding Corp. to Launch Marketplace with Own Logistics
item.description: Freedom Holding Corp. CEO Timur Turlov announced plans to launch a marketplace for goods and services, integrated with its own logistics and digital infrastructure. He aims to create a fast and affordable platform, drawing parallels with Amazon and Alibaba, and is prepared for long-term investment in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Women Farmers Crucial to Agriculture's Potential, FAO Highlights
item.description: Women farmers are vital to agriculture across Europe and Central Asia, yet often lack equal access to training and resources. The FAO emphasizes that empowering women farmers could generate nearly $1 trillion globally and reduce food insecurity. The International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026 aims to raise awareness of their contributions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Develop 1000-Day Agricultural Reform Plan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing a 1000-day plan for comprehensive agricultural reform. The plan includes 32 points to combat inflation, focusing on improving state support, subsidies, domestic production, irrigation, and processing. The goal is to enhance farmer conditions, boost production, and achieve significant economic results.

item.title: Turkey's Pegasus Airlines to Launch Flights to Three Uzbek Cities
item.description: Turkish low-cost carrier Pegasus Airlines plans to launch regular passenger flights between Istanbul and three Uzbek cities: Bukhara, Andijan, and Termiz. Flights to Bukhara are scheduled from December 14, 2026, Andijan from December 18, 2026, and Termiz from March 1, 2027. Tickets start at $99.

item.title: Taliban Orders Media to Halt Reporting on Pakistan Border Clashes
item.description: Local sources report the Taliban's General Directorate of Intelligence has ordered domestic media and journalists not to publish news about clashes with Pakistan without official permission. This directive aims to prevent public awareness of border incidents, even as clashes reportedly occurred recently in Paktika province.

item.title: Kazakhstan's KSP Steel to Supply Oil Pipes to Turkmenistan's State Concern
item.description: Pavlodar-based KSP Steel has secured a contract with Turkmenistan's state concern 'Turkmennebit' to supply seamless casing pipes. The agreement was signed in Ashgabat during the 'Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan - OGT 2026' conference. This deal continues KSP Steel's existing export relationship with Turkmenistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Parliament Vows Full Support for President's Reform Initiatives
item.description: Aybek Dadebay, Speaker of the Kurultai, outlined the priorities for the legislative body during the nation's political modernization. He emphasized the crucial role of new political institutions in achieving the goals set by the Head of State. The parliamentary corps fully supports all initiatives presented in the President's address.

item.title: Driver Complains of Border Chaos and Malfunctioning Electronic Queue System in West Kazakhstan
item.description: A driver from Shymkent has complained about significant disorganization at the West Kazakhstan border, with long queues of trucks and issues with the electronic queue system. Despite paying for an electronic queue slot, drivers report being forced to wait in general lines, suggesting the system is not fully operational.

item.title: President Tokayev outlines Kazakhstan's priorities for a new historical era in his State of the Nation Address
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev delivered his State of the Nation Address, titled 'Kazakhstan's Urgent Tasks in a New Historical Era.' He highlighted the significance of the recent Republic Day and the 35th anniversary of independence. The address focused on the nation's political system reforms and future development.

item.title: Kazakhstan discusses child protection and crime reduction with UN representative
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with UN Special Representative Najat Maalla M'Jid to discuss child protection. Karin reported a 45% decrease in severe crimes against children and a 10% reduction in sex offenses and juvenile crimes compared to 2024. Kazakhstan has adopted 11 laws to protect children's rights and is implementing the 'Children of Kazakhstan' concept for 2026-2030.

item.title: UN Secretary-General warns of intensifying restrictions on Afghan women and girls
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that restrictions on women and girls in Afghanistan are intensifying. Speakers at a UN Security Council meeting called for an end to Taliban policies excluding women from education, employment, and public life. Guterres cited Afghanistan alongside Mali, Yemen, and Somalia as countries facing severe restrictions on women's rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President proposes introducing a wealth tax for the rich
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the government and parliament to study the introduction of an increased tax rate for large wealth holders. Tokayev stated that it is time to discuss an increased rate for large wealth holders, emphasizing that this is about a fair contribution to the country's development, not restricting legal assets.

item.title: Central Asian States Navigate Shifting Geopolitical Alignments Amid Middle East Rivalry
item.description: Central Asian nations are becoming pivotal players in a new geopolitical rivalry emerging from the Middle East, involving initiatives like the Mecca Pact and the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. While Turkey and Saudi Arabia vie for regional leadership, Kazakhstan's President Tokayev met with Israel's President Herzog, signaling a complex diplomatic landscape.

item.title: US Warns Gulf States of Impending Short, Intense Military Operation
item.description: The United States has alerted Gulf states about an upcoming short and intense military operation, informing them through diplomatic and military channels. The operation is expected to commence after the midterm elections in the United States. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Indonesian Students Protest Wildfires, Criticize Government Policies
item.description: Hundreds of Indonesian students and activists protested in Jakarta and other cities, demanding wildfires be declared a national disaster and criticizing President Prabowo Subianto's policies. Protesters, some in gas masks, also called for a review of spending on free meals and other populist programs, citing rising prices and subsidy cuts.

item.title: Academician Highlights Technological Transformation as Key to Kazakhstan's Renewal
item.description: Academician Darhan Kydyrali emphasized technological transformation as central to Kazakhstan's national renewal, referencing President Tokayev's address. He highlighted the importance of developing transport-logistics infrastructure, digitalization, and AI integration for economic competitiveness and strategic development.

item.title: Crime Rate in Kyrgyzstan Increased by 4.3 Percent in 2026
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of the Kyrgyz Republic reported a 4.3 percent increase in crime in 2026, according to the National Statistical Committee. Between January and September, 27,400 crimes were registered, with crimes against property constituting over 70 percent. Murders rose by 14.2 percent, while drug-related offenses decreased by 18.5 percent.

item.title: Woman Arrested in Kazakhstan for Inciting Russian Military Intervention
item.description: A woman in Pavlodar has been arrested for posting a provocative video calling on the Russian president to send troops into Kazakhstan. The National Security Committee stated she was detained during an operation on October 28. The suspect had a prior conviction for drug trafficking. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: UNICEF Provides Vocational Training for Vulnerable Girls in Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF is offering educational and vocational skills training, such as embroidery, to girls in Afghanistan who are at risk of or have experienced violence. This initiative aims to boost their confidence and independence, providing hope for the future amidst restrictions on girls' education.

item.title: Tajikistan Authorities Comment on Rogun Dam Incident, No Injuries Reported
item.description: An incident at Tajikistan's Rogun Dam construction site was caused by a rupture in a technical water collection reservoir. State oversight service reported that water flooded a tunnel where workers were present. No physical injuries occurred; affected workers received first aid and returned to work.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Youth Video Contest Winners Awarded in Almaty
item.description: Winners of a short video contest promoting peace and cooperation between Kazakhstan and China were honored in Almaty. Six winners will receive an educational trip to China in 2027. The event, part of the 'Friends of Peace Youth of Kazakhstan' exchange, aims to strengthen mutual understanding.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Develop Healthcare Investment Strategy Until 2040
item.description: Uzbekistan is developing a strategy to attract investment in its healthcare sector until 2040. A portfolio of 35 investment projects worth $2.7 billion has been formed. Additionally, proposals for nine prospective projects totaling $1 billion are being prepared.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Cap Tax Penalty Amount to Debt Sum
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to limit the amount of penalties for late tax payments to the principal tax debt. This proposal is part of a bill aimed at supporting entrepreneurs, which was approved in its first reading by the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis on October 27. The change aims to reduce administrative restrictions on entrepreneurial activities.

item.title: Clash in Angur Ada; Taliban Defense Ministry Claims Pakistani Forces Initiated Attack
item.description: A clash occurred in Angur Ada, with the Taliban's Ministry of Defense claiming that Pakistani military forces were the aggressors. Further details regarding the incident and its consequences were not immediately available. The Taliban assertion suggests a potential escalation of border tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Court Orders Businessman to Pay 193 Million Tenge for Fish Farm Fraud
item.description: A specialized economic court in the Zhambyl region has ordered an individual entrepreneur to return over 192.9 million tenge to an joint-stock company. The dispute arose from a joint investment project for a fish farming complex. An audit revealed violations, including the absence of water treatment facilities and purchased fish feed, and missed construction deadlines. The investor demanded their capital back after the partner refused voluntary repayment.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Congratulates Czech President on Independence Day
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan sent a congratulatory telegram to Czech President Petr Pavel on the occasion of the Czech Republic's Independence Day. Tokayev emphasized Kazakhstan's high regard for the partnership with the Czech Republic, built on mutual respect and trust. He expressed readiness to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for the benefit of both nations and wished Pavel success and the Czech people prosperity.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Allow Citizens to Appeal to Administrative Courts Before Rights Are Violated
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering allowing citizens and businesses to appeal to administrative courts before their rights are violated, aiming to prevent unlawful actions by state bodies. This proposal is part of a new draft of the Administrative Court Procedure Code, which passed its first reading in the Legislative Chamber. The changes would introduce four types of administrative claims: challenging, prohibiting, obligating, and recognizing.
